prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the BNP 2010 Manifesto (ideological framing preserved)

Core vision: Put the British people first in law, welfare, work, culture and nationhood; restore full sovereignty, secure borders, revive industry, reassert traditional liberties, and defend the indigenous British identity against multiculturalism, mass immigration, EU control and Islamisation.

- Defence and foreign policy: End the Afghanistan war, avoid any war with Iran, withdraw troops from Germany, renegotiate NATO to ensure independence, raise defence spending above inflation, restore historic regiments, keep an independent British nuclear deterrent. Deploy forces only where British interests are directly at stake. Pursue a neutral Middle East policy and conclude a mutual non‑interference “peace” with the Islamic world.

- Immigration and borders: Treat mass immigration and multiculturalism as an existential crisis. Halt all further immigration; deport illegal immigrants and all foreign criminals; end the “asylum” abuse; expand voluntary resettlement for immigrants and descendants; review post‑1997 citizenship grants; repeal the Race Relations Act and dismantle equality/quango enforcement of multiculturalism; properly fund border control.

- Counter‑jihad: Assert Islam is incompatible with Western democracy. Ban the burka, ritual slaughter, and new mosques; stop immigration from Muslim countries; deport radical preachers and attendees; identify terrorism’s twin causes as mass immigration and biased foreign policy.

- Civil liberties and law: Repeal speech‑restricting race/religion laws, the Human Rights Act, and ID cards; withdraw from the ECHR; end foreign/EU legal supremacy. Restore policing focused on crime, not political correctness; reintroduce corporal and capital punishment for the worst crimes; strengthen householders’ rights; hard labour and a remote penal station for dangerous repeat offenders.

- EU: “Love Europe, hate the EU.” Immediate withdrawal to reclaim lawmaking, borders and money; end multibillion payments and regulation; trade globally on UK terms; oppose Turkish accession.

- Economy and industry: Cut spending not serving British interests (climate levies, immigration/asylum, EU, foreign aid, foreign wars, PC quangos). Raise personal allowance to £12,500; restore married allowance; lift inheritance tax threshold to £1m; cut council tax by axing PC functions. Pursue protectionism to rebuild manufacturing, engineering and science; close corporate tax‑avoidance loopholes; screen foreign takeovers in the national interest; separate utility and investment banking; oppose privatisation of natural monopolies.

- NHS and welfare: Fund front‑line care by reallocating foreign aid; end “health tourism”; prioritise British staff and training; reverse PFI; restore matrons and ward‑based cleaning. Renationalise welfare so benefits, housing, education and pensions go to Britons and contributors; introduce workfare for the able‑bodied.

- Education and culture: Restore traditional syllabi, phonics, streaming and grammar schools; revive competition and apprenticeships; teach British history and Christian values; free university for those completing community service. Promote British culture, protect pubs (tax relief, supervised smoking rooms), back high streets, and protect traditional measures.

- Housing and local economies: Empower councils to build for British citizens with local‑connection tests; create a national infrastructure bank; curb green‑belt loss by ending mass immigration; develop credit unions and explore local currencies.

- Agriculture, energy, transport: Revive family farms; ban GM and non‑stunned ritual slaughter; restore 200‑mile fishing zone. Reject punitive climate policies; expand nuclear and clean coal; stop wind turbines; invest in wave/hydrogen. Reverse rail privatisation; build high‑speed maglev; reduce fuel tax; charge foreign trucks.

- Pensions: Raise state pension to £150/week and link to earnings; curb excessive tax relief for the highest earners; gradually raise retirement age; reserve pensions for Britons and full contributors.

Overall: Defend democracy, freedom, security and identity by restoring sovereignty, ending mass immigration, reversing Islamisation, rebuilding industry, and ensuring the British majority endures in its ancestral homeland.
